body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Monday, August 17, 2026, and we’re starting the week with a high near 99° and air quality at a moderate 59. Overnight, the city saw a pair of concerning gun-related incidents, including a report of juveniles brandishing a firearm on Monterey Street. Let’s take a look at the night, the weather, and the stories shaping our day.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious calls involved firearms. Around 11 p.m., a group of five juveniles — one of whom pointed a gun at the reporting party — was reported on Monterey Street. The caller noted that one of the youths claimed a gang affiliation, and all were described as wearing dark clothing. No shots were reported, and units were responding as the feed moved on. Earlier in the evening, shortly before 9:40 p.m., a possible shots-fired incident had units checking local hospitals for gunshot victims and looking for a suspect vehicle, though the exact location remained unclear on the air.

Elsewhere, fire crews handled a one-acre grass fire near the bike path off Oak Street. The fire, which had a slow rate of spread, was accessed from Oak Street, and crews pulled an additional line. In other incidents, multiple units responded to a domestic violence call in progress on Animas Court at 9:54 p.m., and an ex-boyfriend reportedly smashed a vehicle windshield with a shotgun in the FoodMaxx parking lot on Ming Avenue around 11:03 p.m. The reporting party was standing by in that case. Later, at 11:33 p.m., a possible burglary at a Manhattan Drive residence — where a sliding back door was found shattered — had deputies investigating.

The log also noted a vehicle fire inside a tow yard around 12:04 a.m., though the exact location was unclear on the air. Other calls included an alarm at the AutoZone on Ming Avenue at 9:55 p.m., where video showed someone enter and leave as the store was closing; a reckless driver on southbound I-5 north of Lebec around 10:03 p.m., described as a gray/silver sedan weaving and brake-checking; and a medical aid at the Pacific Palms Apartments on O Street around 10:12 p.m., with police also en route. The night also saw a verbal disturbance in the Baker Street area around 10:18 p.m., a medical aid at a residence on Covey Avenue around 10:25 p.m., a possible overdose at the Bank of America on Coffee Road around 10:52 p.m., a small fire on the riverbed at Yokuts Park around 10:58 p.m., a suicidal subject in the South Chester Avenue area around 11:09 p.m., and a welfare check at Applecreek Court involving a young child around 11:19 p.m.

## Today's weather

Today’s forecast calls for a high near 99° and a low around 73° tonight. It’s currently 81° at Meadows Field (KBFL). There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and air quality is at a moderate 59. Enjoy the day, and stay cool if you’re out and about.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Robert F. Kennedy Jr. recently toured a Bakersfield program that he believes could reshape how schools teach children about food, health, and nutrition. Kennedy visited Edible Schoolyard Kern County, which brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum. Students grow their own food in school gardens and then use that fresh produce in kitchen lessons. Congressman Vince Fong noted that the hands-on approach makes the program unique and scalable, not only for schools in the Central Valley but across the country. Kennedy pointed to the program’s focus on fresh food, including school cafeterias buying fresh produce, as an example of how schools can change the way children eat without spending more money. He also highlighted improved testing scores at participating schools, saying the program affects behavior and performance.

**According to 23ABC,** Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Bakersfield Fire Department Chief Kevin Albertson said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state, with significant injuries and even deaths from fireworks. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works, and both departments agreed that stronger measures must be created to decrease fireworks-related accidents and fires.

**23ABC also told us that** Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, recently traveled to San Diego to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development. Baldovinos said one of the most debated topics during the two-day Washington meeting was how long recovery should last, and he pushed back on the view that recovery should only be for a treatment program, noting that in his experience, recovery is a long-term process with people.

## Something good

On a brighter note, Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s recent tour of a Bakersfield program highlights an innovative approach to education and nutrition in our community. The initiative, which brings gardening and cooking into the school curriculum, not only connects what students learn in the classroom to what ends up on their plates but also shows promising results in testing scores and behavior. It’s a reminder of the creative solutions taking root right here in Kern County.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets today, August 18, at 12:00 p.m. The Historic Preservation Commission also meets today at 4:00 p.m. Tomorrow, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. On Wednesday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. And on the same day, the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets at 2:00 p.m.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full lineup this week. On August 22, catch Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, and Grupo Yndio. On August 27, Rodney Carrington takes the stage. August 28 brings Cumbiatron: The Cumbia Rave, and on August 29, Willie Barcena performs alongside the Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. Finally, on September 4, the Mi Historia Tour Leyendas del Mariachi USA comes to town. Enjoy your week, Bakersfield.
